To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) data decomposition, data reorganization and communication analysis techniques can improve locality, reduce cache effects and eliminate barrier synchronization in shared address space machines; 2) the effectiveness of these techniques is similar for shared and distributed machines; 3) the overhead of the techniques is small and can be hidden by parallel speedups.
the use of data decomposition and reorganization transformations can improve performance of shared address space machines by reducing cache conflicts.
the use of unified compilation techniques can improve performance by a factor of 1.6-4.5 on an SGI Origin 2000 shared memory multiprocessor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a unified compilation framework for shared and distributed memory machines that exploits the similarities and differences between the two architectures.
the following question: How can we improve the performance of programs for shared address space parallel machines by exploiting techniques that were developed for distributed memory machines?
the following questions: (1) What are the sources of parallel performance overhead in shared address space machines?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the techniques we describe are very effective at improving performance on both shared and distributed address machines.
the convergence of compilation techniques is an emerging trend that is likely to become more important as parallel machines become more widely used.

these unified compilation techniques can be very effective at improving performance of shared address space machines, especially when used in conjunction with automatic data decomposition and communication analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the convergence of shared and distributed address spaces is a reality.
shared address space machines can achieve scalable performance if their compilers use techniques that were developed for distributed address space architectures.

we have developed techniques that can be used to improve locality, reduce synchronization, and improve performance on shared address space machines by exploiting the same kinds of information and transformations that are used in distributed address space machines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the techniques used to compile distributed address space programs can be used to improve the performance of shared address space programs, and vice versa.

the techniques used in the compilation of programs for distributed address space systems can also be applied to the compilation of programs that are targeted for shared address space parallel machines.
the techniques developed for distributed address space parallel machines can be very useful for improving the scalability of shared address space parallel machines.
